newsitem.title: INDIA: India ruling coalition says confident of solution.
newsitem.headline: India ruling coalition says confident of solution.

text.p: India's ruling United Front, holding crucial talks with its rival Congress party, said on Wednesday it was confident they would resolve a political impasse that has threatened the 10-month old government.
"We are confident of a solution," United Front working president Sharad Yadav told reporters during a brief break in talks with Congress leaders in the Indian capital.
Members of both delegations posed together for photographers, smiling and looking cheerful.

"We are optimistic, that is why we are talking," United Front leader Chandrababu Naidu said. "It is a good beginning," said Farooq Abdullah, chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir state, a member of the ruling alliance.
There was no immediate comment from the Congress delegates.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who has depended on Congress support to survive a challenge by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party, was due to face a vote of confidence in parliament on Friday.
